diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely over 0-255 per entry. Emit 0 in most files, since that is what real writers produce, but include a share of non-zero values so alpha-confusing decoders are exercised.
diversity_axes.notes: Tier C. Distinct from RGBQUAD at 32 bpp, where the same byte position is a real alpha channel inside BITMAPLINE.colors.

diversity_axes.name: direct_colour_pixel_bytes
diversity_axes.why: At 24 bpp each pixel is one RGBTRIPLE (line 129), so these three bytes are the whole image content and are entirely free. This is where per-pixel coverage comes from for the most common depth: solid fills, gradients, checkerboards and high-entropy noise each drive different conversion and dithering paths.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The 3-byte-per-pixel row copy, BGR-to-RGB channel reordering, and any colour conversion or dithering applied when the display depth is lower.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw each channel byte independently and uniformly over 0-255 for every pixel of every row, with no correlation between neighbouring pixels. Seed a few structured images into the corpus (all-zero, all-0xFF, horizontal gradient, single-channel noise) so both random and degenerate pixel data appear.
diversity_axes.notes: Tier C. RGBTRIPLE is the 3-byte record; the 4-byte RGBQUAD variant at 32 bpp is covered by BITMAPLINE.colors.

diversity_axes.name: sub_byte_pixel_packing
diversity_axes.why: At depths below 8 the row is a packed byte array (line 125) whose bits are MSB-first palette indices, so the content is free but its interpretation is a real encoding rule. This axis drives the bit-extraction loop, the handling of indices that fall outside a short palette, and the interaction between the last partial byte of a row and the mandatory padding.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: MSB-first bit extraction at 1, 2 and 4 bpp, the shift/mask sequence per pixel, the end-of-row partial-byte case, and the palette bounds check on every extracted index.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Fill rowBytes bytes with uniformly random content, then additionally seed structured rows into the corpus: all indices 0, all indices at the palette maximum, an index ramp that wraps, and rows whose final partial byte is non-zero so the padding boundary is exercised. Also include a share of out-of-range indices as a malformed class.
diversity_axes.notes: Recorded as a payload_wellformedness constraint because the bytes are free but their packing is not: the generator must pack MSB-first and must not let biWidth disagree with rowBytes.

diversity_axes.name: index_per_byte_pixels
diversity_axes.why: At 8 bpp the row is one palette index per byte across biWidth bytes (line 127), so the content is free while the count and the index-to-palette relationship are not. This is the most common indexed depth and the one both RLE codecs target, so its content axis matters for coverage of palette lookup.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The one-byte-per-pixel row copy, palette lookup per pixel, and the index bounds check against the palette entry count.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit exactly biWidth bytes per row, drawn uniformly over 0-255. Seed structured rows as well (all 0, all 255, an ascending ramp, runs of a single index) so both random and RLE-like content appear, plus a share of indices above the palette size as a malformed class.
diversity_axes.notes: The array length is derived from biWidth and is not itself an axis; only the byte values are free.

diversity_axes.name: direct_colour_pixel_records
diversity_axes.why: At 24 and 32 bpp the row is an array of biWidth RGBTRIPLE or RGBQUAD records (lines 129-131). The record count is derived from biWidth, but the choice of 3-byte versus 4-byte record and the bytes inside it are the whole image content, and a wrong record size desynchronises every offset after it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The per-pixel record copy at 3 or 4 bytes, BGR versus BGRA channel ordering, and at 32 bpp the alpha-blending path that the fourth byte enables.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit exactly biWidth records of the size the depth selects, with every channel byte drawn uniformly over 0-255. At 32 bpp vary the alpha byte across the full range too, including 0 and 255, so opaque and fully transparent pixels both appear. Seed structured images (solid, gradient, checkerboard) alongside random noise.
diversity_axes.notes: With BI_BITFIELDS the masks, not the depth alone, decide which bits are which channel; keep the emitted bytes consistent with the masks chosen.

diversity_axes.name: row_alignment_padding
diversity_axes.why: Every row is padded to a 4-byte boundary (lines 116-118, 134-135), and the padding count is derived from rowBytes while the padding bytes themselves are free. Flipping them between zero and non-zero is a cheap, high-value probe of whether a decoder actually skips the padding or consumes it as pixel data.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The row-advance step, the alignment skip, and the desynchronisation that follows if a decoder ignores padding.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit exactly padding bytes per row, where padding is 0 when rowBytes is already a multiple of 4. Draw the padding byte values freely over 0-255 rather than always zeroing them, so the corpus contains rows whose padding is non-zero and therefore detects any decoder that reads past rowBytes.
diversity_axes.notes: The count is a format rule, not an axis; only the byte values are free. Rows with padding == 0 must emit nothing at all.

diversity_axes.name: scanline_array
diversity_axes.why: The second repeating structure and the uncompressed pixel region itself: |biHeight| rows back to back with no framing (line 137). Its repetition count is the axis that most changes file size and shape, and the row order is a genuine decoder branch.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The row iteration loop, bottom-up versus top-down row addressing, the per-row stride computation, and the truncation check when fewer bytes remain than the declared row count requires.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Derive the row count from |biHeight| and emit exactly that many rows at a constant stride of rowBytes + padding. Vary the shape of the image freely - tall and thin, wide and short, square, single-row, single-column - and vary the sign of biHeight independently so both row orders appear. Never emit fewer rows than declared.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Pixel-data output_budget 4 MiB across the whole file, kept by redrawing the biWidth/biHeight pair until stride * |biHeight| fits; never by clamping the emitted dimensions and never by truncating the row array. 4 MiB still admits 4096x1024 at 8 bpp, 1024x4096, 2048x2048 and 640x480 at 24 bpp, so the budget does not bias the width, height, aspect-ratio or depth distribution.
diversity_axes.notes: Mutually exclusive with GLOBAL.rleData; exactly one of the two exists per file.

diversity_axes.name: encoded_pixel_payload
diversity_axes.why: The only genuinely compressed or externally-encoded payload in the format, and the .bt says nothing about it beyond sizing a bare UBYTE array (lines 108 and 110). Its content is the highest-value axis in the whole specification: the generator chooses the runs, the deltas, the escape mix, where the terminator lands, or whether the region is an embedded JPEG or PNG at all.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The RLE8 and RLE4 state machines - encoded-mode pairs, escape 0x00 with sub-codes 0x00 (end of line), 0x01 (end of bitmap), 0x02 (delta) and 0x03 (absolute run), the odd-length absolute-run padding rule, and the row/column advance against the declared biWidth and biHeight. For BI_JPEG and BI_PNG the region is handed to a completely different decoder, with its own markers, chunks and CRCs.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Build the payload from the declared biWidth, biHeight and biBitCount - never the reverse - and vary every aspect of it: long and short runs, single-pixel runs, every escape sub-code, deltas that move down and right, deltas that would leave the image bounds, absolute runs of odd and even length, terminators placed early or omitted, and streams that end without a terminator so the decoder must fall back on biSizeImage. For BI_JPEG and BI_PNG emit a real minimal embedded image, plus truncated and corrupt variants. Include a share of well-formed streams whose decoded size disagrees with the declared dimensions, which is the classic malformed-BMP class.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Shares the single 4 MiB pixel-data output_budget with GLOBAL.lines; the budget applies to the encoded byte count, which is then written into biSizeImage and included in bfSize.
diversity_axes.notes: Recorded as payload_wellformedness because the format defines a codec here that the template does not describe. The payload must be derived from the declared dimensions; adjusting biWidth or biHeight to match a payload the generator happened to produce inverts the dependency and destroys the axis.

diversity_axes.name: reserved_header_words
diversity_axes.why: Two 16-bit words the specification calls reserved and the template never reads, so they are unconstrained entropy that costs nothing to vary. They probe whether a decoder wrongly validates reserved fields and measure how much of a file a consumer actually inspects.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: None in conforming decoders.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw each word freely over 0-65535. Emit 0 in most files, since that is what real writers produce, but include a share of non-zero values so any decoder that mistakenly checks them is caught.
diversity_axes.notes: Tier C. Distinct from RGBQUAD.rgbReserved, which is a per-entry reserved byte inside the colour table.

diversity_axes.name: physical_resolution
diversity_axes.why: Purely advisory metadata that no structural check depends on, so it is a safe free axis. Real files carry 0, 2835 (72 dpi) or 3780 (96 dpi); negative, zero and absurd values test whether a decoder scales the image or ignores the field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The physical-size reporting path and any DPI-based scaling a viewer applies; no pixel decoding depends on it.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw each LONG freely over its whole range, including negative values. Seed the common real-world values 0, 2835 and 3780 into the corpus so typical files appear, and vary the two fields independently so asymmetric resolutions occur.
diversity_axes.notes: Tier C: the format treats these as hints, so no generation range may be recorded.

diversity_axes.name: important_colour_count
diversity_axes.why: An advisory count of how many palette entries actually matter, with a soft ceiling at the palette size and no structural effect. Spanning 0 (all colours important), small values and the full palette size exercises the code path where a decoder optimises for a partial palette or builds a reduced colour cube.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The palette-importance check and any partial-palette optimisation; conforming decoders otherwise ignore it.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely over the DWORD range: 0 in most files, then values up to the palette entry count, plus a share of values above it as a malformed class. At 24/32 bpp emit 0.
diversity_axes.notes: Tier C. Its soft ceiling is recorded as a dependency, not as a generation range on this field.

diversity_axes.name: info_header_size
diversity_axes.why: Listed as a protection note: the value is pinned to 40 because this template declares exactly one 40-byte BITMAPINFOHEADER, and it also determines where the next region starts. The rewrite step must not treat it as a diversity axis, but it should know that other legal values (12, 52, 56, 108, 124) select header variants this template does not model.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The header-variant dispatch that real decoders perform on this field, and the offset computation for everything after the header.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Never: emit 40 in every file this generator produces. If a header variant is ever wanted it must come with the extra fields that variant defines, which is outside this template's scope.
diversity_axes.notes: Tier A fixed_value with calculated_value metadata attached, since the field is simultaneously a literal and the byte count of the structure it sizes.

diversity_axes.name: colour_plane_count
diversity_axes.why: Another protection note: the specification requires exactly 1 and at least one widely used decoder aborts with 'invalid planes' on any other value. Pinning it costs zero diversity, since no decoder branches usefully on a second plane, so the rewrite step must not vary it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The plane-count validation check that some decoders perform before touching pixel data; nothing else reads the field.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Never: emit 1 (bytes 01 00) in every file.
diversity_axes.notes: Close call between Tier A and Tier C, resolved as Tier A because the format rule is unconditional and the field is unread by the template; the reasoning is recorded on the constraint entry.
